title: Next-year heat gave no clear bleaching link in four matched Atlantic and Pacific coral samples in 2003-2018
abstract: We tested next-year heat stress as a check on coral bleaching associations. We matched the same site and calendar month in consecutive years within 2003-2010 and 2011-2019. Four Atlantic and Pacific models used 840 monthly records and controlled current heat, depth, site, year and month. Future heat slopes were +5.01, -0.85, -0.61 and +1.60 bleaching percentage points per four TSA degree-heating weeks. All four country-cluster intervals included zero after adjustment for four comparisons. Ecological-region, year and site-by-month checks also gave no clear future link. Only 840 of 7,820 source months met the match and repeat rules. Few clusters, broad intervals, heat persistence and selection on future survey reports limit the test. A null future slope does not show that current heat estimates are free from bias. This study does not estimate pollution effects, species loss or causal climate effects. The package includes code, source hashes, raw-data checks, matched evidence and offline reproduction instructions.

display.caption: Current and next-year accumulated heat slopes in the joint models. Thick lines give nominal 95 percent country-cluster t intervals. Thin lines give four-comparison intervals. All future intervals include zero. Small selected samples and few clusters limit inference.

citations.reason: We reuse its verified monthly panel and independently reconstruct all fields from unchanged raw data.
Prior before-versus-after monthly temperature test. We extend the diagnostic to next-year accumulated heat on exact same-site calendar-month matches.
